traceability.evidence:
Story file matches the provided specification: - docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md content exactly matches the story in the prompt.
Rule implementation: - src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts - Defines a RuleModule with: - meta.type: "problem" and fixable: "code". - docs.description: "Enforce traceability annotations and naming conventions in test files". - docs.recommended: "error" (meets Quality Standards & Integration criteria). - schema: one options object with properties exactly as in the story: - testFilePatterns?: string[] (default ["/tests/", "/test/", "/__tests__", ".test.", ".spec."]) - requireDescribeStory?: boolean (default true) - requireTestReqPrefix?: boolean (default true) - describePattern?: string (default "Story [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+-") - autoFixTestTemplate?: boolean (default true) - autoFixTestPrefixFormat?: boolean (default true) - testSupportsTemplate?: string - additionalProperties: false. - messages: - missingFileSupports: "Test file must have @supports annotation listing tested requirements." - missingDescribeStory: "describe() block should reference story (e.g., 'Story 009.0-DEV-...')." - missingReqPrefix: "Test name should start with requirement ID (e.g., '[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] ...')." (These match the story’s example error messages.) - create(context): - Reads options with the documented defaults. - Uses determineIsTestFile(filename, testFilePatterns) to decide if a file is a test file (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT). - Returns {} (no visitors) for non-test files, so production code is unaffected. - For test files: - Gets sourceCode and calls ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate }) to enforce file-level @supports (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS, REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID in combination with other rules). - Builds describeRegex from describePattern. - Returns visitors: - CallExpression: handleCallExpression(context, { sourceCode, describeRegex, requireDescribeStory, requireTestReqPrefix, autoFixTestPrefixFormat }). - This implements validation of describe() story references and it()/test() [REQ-...] prefixes, for all (including nested) describes in the file (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY, REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT). - Traceability annotations: - @story docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT - @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
Helper implementation: - src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts - determineIsTestFile(filename, rawPatterns?): - Defaults patterns to ["/tests/", "/test/", "/__tests__", ".test.", ".spec."] and returns true if any substring occurs in filename (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT; matches Implementation Notes patterns, and is configurable via rule options). - ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions): - Checks sourceCode.getAllComments() for any comment whose value matches /@supports\b/. - If missing: - Reports messageId: "missingFileSupports" on the first comment or AST root. - If autoFixTestTemplate !== false, fixer inserts a JSDoc @supports template at the top using insertSupportsTemplate. - insertSupportsTemplate preserves shebang lines and inserts the template right after (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS, REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID, and auto-fix behavior described in Implementation Notes). - buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?): - Default template line: "@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ" followed by a TODO comment, as in the story. - isTestCallName(name): - Returns true for "describe", "it", "test", "context" (REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT and matches Test Framework Compatibility section). - getCalleeName(node): - Supports Identifier and MemberExpression with Identifier object name, so describe.each/test.each work as intended. - handleDescribeCall(context, node, description, { describeRegex, requireDescribeStory }): - If requireDescribeStory and description does not match regex, reports messageId: "missingDescribeStory" (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY). - handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options): - If requireTestReqPrefix is true and description does not match /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/, reports messageId: "missingReqPrefix". - When autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false and normalizeReqPrefixInDescription returns a normalized value and the first argument is a string Literal, attaches a fixer that replaces the literal text with a canonical [REQ-...] prefix while preserving quoting (via createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw). - Implements REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX and safe normalization (details extended in Story 021.0 but required for good error context and auto-fix examples). - handleCallExpression(context, options): - Visitor factory for CallExpression: - Gets calleeName via getCalleeName, filters to test functions via isTestCallName. - Extracts first argument literal as description. - For "describe", invokes handleDescribeCall (enforcing story reference). For "it"/"test", invokes handleItOrTestCall. - Applies to all describes in test files (including nested), fulfilling REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE. - All key helpers are annotated with @supports referencing Story 020.0 and 021.0 with the correct requirement IDs.
Plugin integration: - src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes "require-test-traceability", so the rule is dynamically required and exposed under plugin.rules. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/require-test-traceability" to "error". - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() returns a config with rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES }. - configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()] } and assigned to plugin.configs. - This ensures the rule is enabled by default in both recommended and strict presets at error severity, satisfying "Integration" and "Rule added to recommended configuration" in Definition of Done.
Documentation: - user-docs/api-reference.md - Contains heading: "### traceability/require-test-traceability". - Under configuration presets, lists: "- `traceability/require-test-traceability`: `error`". - Prior validated content (file unchanged in this assessment) documents: - Requirement for file-level @supports annotations in test files. - Requirement for story references in top-level describe blocks. - Requirement for [REQ-XXX] prefixes in it/test names. - Options: testFilePatterns, requireDescribeStory, requireTestReqPrefix, describePattern, autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, testSupportsTemplate. - This matches the story’s Implementation Notes under Configuration Options and fulfills the "Documentation" acceptance criterion.
Tests for the rule: - tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - File header includes @supports mapping Story 020.0 and its requirements plus Story 021.0 auto-fix requirements. - Uses RuleTester with ECMAScript 2020 module settings. - Valid cases: 1) File-level @supports present; describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', ...); it('[REQ-EXAMPLE] ...') in a tests/ filename → passes, confirming that when all patterns (file-level, describe story, REQ prefix) are satisfied, no errors are reported (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS, REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY, REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX). 2) context('Story 020.0-...') in a test file with @supports → accepted, confirming Mocha-style context() support and framework compatibility (REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT). 3) describe('Story 020.0-...', ...) in a non-test filename ("src/not-a-test-file.ts") with @supports → no errors, verifying that non-test files are ignored even if they look like tests (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT). 4) A correctly formatted [REQ-TRACE-123] prefix in test name is accepted unchanged, proving that the rule does not over-fix already-correct prefixes (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT consistency). - Invalid cases: 1) Missing @supports in a test file: - Code: only describe + it with a REQ prefix; filename in tests/. - Expected error: messageId "missingFileSupports". - Expected output: file with a prepended @supports JSDoc template and TODO line, exactly matching the helper’s buildSupportsTemplateComment output. - Verifies file-level validation and auto-fix (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS). 2) Bad describe story reference: - Has @supports but describe('no story reference here', ...). - filename under tests/. - Expected error: messageId "missingDescribeStory" (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY). 3) Missing REQ prefix in test name: - Has @supports but it('missing prefix', () => {}). - Expected error: messageId "missingReqPrefix" with no output fix, confirming conservative behavior when no REQ ID is present (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT & no inference requirement). 4–7) Malformed REQ prefixes: - Variants: '[ REQ-TEST-FIX ]', '[REQ_TEST_FIX]', '[req-lowercase]', '(REQ-PAREN) with parens'. - Each has @supports and is in a tests/ filename. - Expected errors: messageId "missingReqPrefix" with fixed output that normalizes these into '[REQ-TEST-FIX] ...' or '[REQ-LOWERCASE] ...'. - Confirms safe normalization, format enforcement, and fix behavior described under REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX and Implementation Notes (plus Story 021.0’s auto-fix story).
Cross-rule validation for @supports correctness (REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID): - valid-story-reference rule (src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts) with tests in tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts - Validates that story paths in annotations (@story, @supports) correspond to existing files and respect path/boundary constraints. - valid-req-reference rule (src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts) with tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - Validates that requirement IDs used in annotations exist in the referenced story content, including supports-based multi-story patterns. - Both rules are part of RULE_NAMES and are enabled in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES as `error`, so once require-test-traceability enforces presence of @supports in test files, these other rules ensure those @supports are semantically valid, satisfying REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID.
Test execution (this assessment): - Command: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose --testPathPatterns tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - Jest output: - PASS tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - Suite: "require-test-traceability rule (Stories 020.0 and 021.0)" with all 11 tests passing (valid and invalid cases as described above). - Test Suites: 1 passed / 1 total - Tests: 11 passed / 11 total. - Confirms current behavior matches the tests and, through them, the story requirements.
Combined, this evidence shows: - File-level @supports enforcement ✔ - Describe story reference enforcement ✔ - Test-name [REQ-XXX] prefix enforcement and safe normalization ✔ - ESLint best-practice rule design and performance characteristics ✔ - Full integration into the plugin and recommended/strict configs ✔ - Clear, actionable error messages matching the story ✔ - Support for Jest, Mocha, and related frameworks (describe, it, test, context, describe.each/test.each) ✔ - Documented behavior and options in user-docs ✔ - Dependency rules met via reuse of existing validation rules and stories ✔
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md are implemented. The require-test-traceability rule enforces file-level @supports annotations, describe() story references, and [REQ-XXX] prefixes on test names for recognized test files and frameworks, integrates with existing story and requirement validation rules, is enabled in the recommended/strict presets, has clear error messages, and is documented in the user API reference. Dedicated RuleTester tests for this story pass, and supporting rules for story/requirement validation also exist and are enabled. Therefore this story is fully implemented and passing.
